stock.counterargument: Debt is 6.82× trailing operating cash flow, which leaves less room if conditions turn.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +64.1%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $39.79 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-28, 13 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-10.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-24) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.lead: Aprozper said a passive DNS search returned 43,601 links ending in grok.me. Of them, more than 35,000, or nearly 95 percent, were public, meaning that clicking on the link opened the corresponding app and all data it stored. He said that tests he conducted over the past week showed that, by default, Grok sets links to “Anyone with the link.” Users have the option to change the setting to “invited users” or “only you.”

stories.title: Iran-backed trio accused of plotting attacks on U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
stories.excerpt: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.
stories.lead:
Federal prosecutors in New York have charged three men with terrorism offenses over what they describe as an Iran-backed campaign of nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States. The charges include a September plot against a British air base where American forces were stationed.

The indictment, unsealed on Tuesday, names Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, 32, who holds Iranian and Iraqi citizenship, Mohsen Mohajeri, 48, an Iranian, and Mohammed Ali Al-Hassani, 35, an Iraqi.

stories.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now
stories.excerpt: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.
stories.lead:
An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill.

A majority of the House of Representatives voted to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky, for now.

In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage".

stories.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
stories.excerpt: Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease.
stories.lead:
According to the latest health ministry data, 11,042 people have been infected with the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387 — nearly half of those infected in what has been Congo's deadliest outbreak.

The outbreak was declared in mid-May, and since then, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to several factors, including armed conflicts, a health system crisis, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation.

stories.title: Eswatini gives illegal foreign businesses 12 months to leave
stories.excerpt: The law follows the growth of foreign-owned businesses in retail sector in rural areas.
stories.lead:
Businesses owned by Asian nationals are being closed across Eswatini as the government cracks down on foreign-owned enterprises.

The crackdown follows Parliament's approval of the Citizen Economic Empowerment Act, which seeks to increase ownership and participation by emaSwati, as citizens in the kingdom are known.

The legislation follows complaints from local traders that foreign-owned businesses are encroaching on traditional retail markets, increasing competition and threatening livelihoods.

stories.title: Oil giant ExxonMobil left Venezuela years ago. Now it's considering a return
stories.excerpt: ExxonMobil has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and its state-owned oil company to explore opportunities in the country.
stories.lead:
ExxonMobil, the biggest U.S. oil company, is exploring a return to Venezuela after leaving almost two decades ago.

On Monday, the company announced it had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and its state-owned oil company, Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. The MOU, which is typically a non-binding agreement, involves ExxonMobil examining potential "upstream opportunities" – that refers to oil exploration and production.

ExxonMobil said in a statement, "We welcome the opportunity to evaluate potential upstream opportunities with the Venezuelan government and PDVSA."
